Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

As a Fraud and Disputes Vendor Management Specialist, you will be responsible for the day-to-day management and performance of our external operations partners. You’ll serve as a key connection point between internal Operations teams and our vendors, ensuring expectations are clear, performance is understood, and issues are quickly identified and resolved. You’ll use data to monitor SLAs, productivity, quality, staffing, and other key performance indicators while partnering with vendors to develop and execute improvement plans. You’ll also support capacity planning, new program launches, training, and changes to existing operations as our business continues to scale.

Available shift

  • Monday through Friday; 8:00am – 5:00pm CT

This role is based in our Chicago, IL, Denver, CO, Lake Mary, FL and Westlake, TX offices with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Manage day-to-day relationships with external operations partners and serve as a primary point of contact for operational needs.
  • Monitor vendor performance across key metrics including SLA, productivity, quality, customer experience, attendance, and staffing.
  • Lead recurring vendor performance reviews and ensure risks, trends, and opportunities have clear owners and action plans.
  • Partner with Operations leaders and vendors on capacity planning, staffing forecasts, schedules, hiring, and training needs.
  • Identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and partner with vendors to develop and track corrective action plans.
  • Ensure vendors are prepared for new products, processes, policies, tooling changes, and volume growth.
  • Partner with internal teams to communicate business priorities and translate them into clear expectations for vendor teams.
  • Use operational data to identify trends, proactively flag risks, and recommend opportunities to improve performance and efficiency.
  • Support vendor expansions, new lines of business, site launches, and other operational changes.
  • Maintain strong governance and documentation around vendor performance, commitments, escalations, and operational changes.
  • Partner with the Fraud and Disputes Teams, Operations Enablement, Risk, Compliance, Quality, Training, and other teams to ensure vendor operations meet internal standards and requirements.

What you bring

  • 2+ years of experience in vendor management, BPO operations, workforce management, operations, or a related role.
  • Experience managing or partnering with outsourced operations teams is preferred.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience using operational metrics to identify trends and drive performance improvements.
  • Strong understanding of operational KPIs such as SLA, productivity, quality, AHT, utilization, and staffing.
  • Experience with capacity planning, forecasting, staffing, or workforce management is a plus.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external partners.
  • Ability to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and hold partners accountable to clear action plans.
  • Experience working in financial services, fintech, fraud, disputes, customer support, or another regulated environment is a plus.
  • Experience with Salesforce, reporting tools, workforce management platforms, or other operational systems is a plus.

The Role

As a Sales Manager, you'll lead a team of Account Executives and own one of our most critical growth levers in-market: developing talent that consistently outperforms while helping Japanese sellers succeed. This role is about building a high-performance sales organization where every hire raises the bar, every coaching conversation sharpens execution, and every decision is grounded in data — all within the realities of the Japanese market.

You'll operate at the intersection of local and global. You'll adapt our global playbooks to how deals are actually won in Japan — where trust is earned over time, decisions are made by consensus, and relationships matter as much as the commercial case. You'll bring the rigor, along with the energy.

You'll be expected to coach in the work, not after it. You'll diagnose pipeline health before it becomes a forecasting problem, develop future leaders before promotions become necessary, and create an operating rhythm that enables predictable, repeatable growth in a market with long, relationship-driven sales cycles.

You'll partner cross-functionally — locally and with regional/global HQ — to improve how we sell in Japan, challenge the status quo, and continuously raise the talent bar. Success is measured not only by quota attainment, but by the strength of your team, the quality of your pipeline, and the leaders you develop.

Build a High-Performance Team

  • Hire bilingual Account Executives who can run complex, multi-stakeholder deals in-market, and raise the bar with every addition to your team — competing effectively for scarce sales talent in Tokyo.
  • Develop a culture of ownership, accountability, continuous learning and high standards, balanced with the trust and cohesion that Japanese teams are built on.
  • Identify future top performers early and create development plans that accelerate their growth.
  • Ramp and retain talent in a competitive local labour market where strong bilingual sellers have options.

Co-Sell on Complex Deals

  • Sell alongside your team in discovery, business case development and negotiation on your most important pursuits. 
  • Engage senior stakeholders directly — including owners, operations and finance — and help your team multi-thread and navigate consensus-driven, bottom-up decision-making rather than selling to a single champion.
  • Bring commercial judgment to pricing, deal structure and competitive displacement against local players. 
  • Advance the deal while leaving the AE more capable of running the next one without you.

Coach Through Data & Business Intelligence

  • Lead your business through rigorous pipeline inspection, forecasting and performance diagnostics.
  • Use leading indicators to identify performance gaps early and coach reps toward sustainable improvement.
  • Turn data into action by identifying trends, diagnosing root causes and driving measurable improvements across your team.
  • Forecast accurately on long-cycle deals, which depends on stage integrity rather than optimism — and account for local cycle length and relationship-building phases.

Drive Operational Excellence

  • Establish predictable operating rhythms around forecasting, pipeline management and business reviews.
  • Build disciplined execution that creates consistent, repeatable revenue outcomes.
  • Continuously improve how your team sells by refining processes, simplifying execution and eliminating friction.
  • Build repeatable plays for how this segment is won in Japan — from acquisition through implementation and expansion.

Lead Through Influence

  • Partner closely with Sales Leadership, Marketing, Enablement, Operations, Partnerships and Product — locally and at regional/global HQ — to improve the customer journey and strengthen commercial execution.
  • Act as a two-way bridge: bring global best practice into Japan, and bring the Japanese customer voice and field intelligence back to shape strategy and influence product evolution.
  • Use customer insights and local market knowledge to localise strategy for Japan's cashless transition (the national push toward ~65% cashless by 2030) and the merchant landscape.
  • Lead through change by helping your team adapt quickly while maintaining high performance.

You Have

  • 6+ years experience as a sales manager, including time leading teams selling into complex, multi-stakeholder accounts with cycles measured in months.
  • Native or business-level fluency in Japanese, plus professional business-level English — able to lead in-market in Japanese and collaborate effectively with regional/global stakeholders in English.
  • Deep knowledge of the Japanese market — including the Seller landscape, buying behavior, business etiquette, and consensus-based decision-making — and ideally experience in payments, fintech, SaaS or a related B2B category.
  • An understanding of the Japanese cashless/payments environment and competitive dynamics (e.g. QR-code wallets, card networks and bank-led offerings), and how these shape merchant decisions.
  • Experience hiring, ramping and retaining Account Executives who can run considered, competitive deals — ideally within the Japanese talent market.
  • Experience developing already strong performers into people who win larger and more complex deals.
  • Proven track record in collaborating across different teams, including across a local–global structure, with the ability to inspire change.
  • Leadership and coaching experience and a desire to help others be their best.
  • Expertise in creating structure around sales metrics and managing yourself and others to achieve these metrics, including forecast accuracy on long-cycle deals.
  • An understanding of how to refine decision-making and consider the downstream and upstream effects of potential decisions.
  • Experience localising global sales playbooks and enablement for the Japanese market.

Application Guidelines

Candidates may submit up to 9 active applications within a 60-day period. Reapplications to the same role are accepted 90 days after a previous application has been reviewed.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We may use automated AI tools to evaluate job applications for efficiency and consistency. These tools comply with local regulations, including bias audits, and we handle all personal data in accordance with state and local privacy laws. 

Contact us here with hiring practice or data usage questions.

Every benefit we offer is designed with one goal: empowering you to do the best work of your career while building the life you want. Remote work, medical insurance, flexible time off, retirement savings plans, and modern family planning are just some of our offering. Check out our other benefits at Block.

Block, Inc. (NYSE: XYZ) builds technology to increase access to the global economy. Each of our brands unlocks different aspects of the economy for more people. Square makes commerce and financial services accessible to sellers. Cash App is the easy way to spend, send, and store money. Afterpay is transforming the way customers manage their spending over time. TIDAL is a music platform that empowers artists to thrive as entrepreneurs. Bitkey is a simple self-custody wallet built for bitcoin. Proto is a suite of bitcoin mining products and services. Together, we’re helping build a financial system that is open to everyone.

Chainlink Labs is one of the primary contributing developers of Chainlink, the standard for onchain finance enabling high-quality data, secure cross-chain interoperability, and compliant connectivity across global markets. Chainlink powers leading tokenized assets, financial institutions, market infrastructures, and decentralized applications by providing secure access to real-world data, cross-chain messaging, and blockchain connectivity across any network. The Chainlink standard has enabled tens of trillions of dollars in transaction value and is helping unify global markets onchain. Many of the world’s largest financial services institutions have also adopted Chainlink’s standards and infrastructure, including Swift, Euroclear, Mastercard, Fidelity International, UBS, S&P Dow Jones Indices, FTSE Russell, WisdomTree, ANZ, Aave, Polymarket, Lido, and many others.

Chainlink Labs is a world-class team of developers, researchers, and capital markets experts, and has ranked among Fortune's Best Workplaces in Technology, Fortune's Best Medium Workplace, and the Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces. Learn more at chain.link or chainlinklabs.com.

Chainlink Labs is looking for a Sales lead to build and scale a new institutional offering that helps financial institutions launch and operate digital asset initiatives through a unified, Chainlink-led approach. You will shape how banks, asset managers, custodians, and financial market infrastructures access the technology and services needed to bring global finance on-chain.

Institutions today navigate complex integrations across custody, tokenization, legacy systems, compliance, and cross-chain distribution. Working across Chainlink’s capabilities and partner ecosystem, you will help define an offering that brings these components together, validate where demand is strongest, and turn that demand into commercial opportunities.

This is a hands-on commercial leadership role with a mandate to build a new business from the ground up. You will define priority customer segments, shape pricing and packaging, and personally lead the first strategic deals.

Your Impact

  • Define and execute the go-to-market strategy for a unified digital asset infrastructure offering (“one stop shop”), establishing priority markets, customer profiles, target accounts, and a clear value proposition.

  • Lead structured discovery with senior institutional stakeholders to understand their business priorities, buying committees, budget ownership, and requirements for adoption.

  • Identify and prioritize the strongest commercial opportunities across tokenized assets, tokenized deposits, custody connectivity, institutional data, compliance, and cross-chain distribution.

  • Personally originate, advance, and close flagship customer deals, working alongside internal account owners to build executive alignment and navigate complex sales cycles.

  • Develop scalable pricing, packaging, services models, and partner economics that meet institutional needs and support a repeatable commercial offering.

  • Partner with Product, Solutions Architecture, Legal, Marketing, and Partnerships to align customer requirements with technical scope, commercial terms, and market positioning.

  • Turn early opportunities and customer wins into sales playbooks, qualification criteria, and enablement materials that equip the broader BCM Sales organization to scale adoption.

  • Demonstrated success building a new commercial offering, go-to-market motion, or business line from initial market validation through early revenue and repeatable growth.

  • Deep understanding of institutional digital asset infrastructure, including tokenization, custody, stablecoins, interoperability, and compliance, and how these capabilities address institutional needs.

  • Proven ability to engage C-level stakeholders and personally close complex, multi-million-dollar deals with financial institutions.

  • Strong commercial judgment, with the ability to assess market demand, prioritize opportunities, and translate customer insight into compelling propositions and commercial models.

  • A hands-on, player-coach approach, combining direct ownership of strategic deals with the ability to establish processes and enable other sellers.

  • Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and bring structure to ambiguous opportunities, aligning technical and commercial stakeholders around clear priorities and execution.

About the Company:

Tools for Humanity (TFH) designs and builds technology behind World. World is building a real human network designed to accelerate people in the age of AI. As bots and autonomous agents reshape the internet, people, institutions, and applications need a trusted way to confirm who is a real human while preserving privacy. The TFH and World tech stacks make this possible: the Orb verifies real, unique people, World ID proves it privately, and World App puts these capabilities, and more, in people’s hands. Together, they add a human layer to an AI-driven internet.

World is already running at a global scale. More than 17 million people across 160 countries have verified with World ID, and more new Orb verifications take place each week. World App is already among the most used wallets globally. Developers are integrating World ID to build safer online experiences and create spaces where real people can participate, earn, and be recognized in ways AI simply can’t replicate.

Founded in 2019, TFH has more than 400 people across hardware, software, AI, cryptography, mobile engineering, and global operations. Our teams come from OpenAI, Tesla, SpaceX, Apple, Google, Stripe, Meta, Coinbase, Palantir and MIT Media Lab. We’re backed by leading investors, including a16z, Khosla Ventures, Bain Capital Crypto, Blockchain Capital, Variant, Tiger Global, and Coinbase Ventures, as well as prominent operators and founders across fintech and AI.

TFH and World have been featured on the cover of TIME Magazine, highlighted in Fast Company’s Next 5 in Fintech, and explored in a Bloomberg deep dive. The New York Times, Bankless and TechCrunch have all recognized our collective progress in identity, cryptography, AI, and global-scale hardware deployment. Our leadership is also named to the Time AI 100. Learn more about the newest product launches from our Liftoff event.

About the Team

The Security team at Tools for Humanity operates at a level far beyond a regular company. Our objective is not just to secure an organization, but to build the trusted, foundational infrastructure for the world's largest identity and financial network. Our seasoned engineers are central to the success of the World protocol. We tackle a unique and complex threat landscape that spans state-of-the-art hardware security for the Orb, advanced cryptography including new zero-knowledge proofs, and the security of a global, distributed cloud and mobile ecosystem. Our work is critical to enabling the protocol to scale to billions of users while upholding an unwavering commitment to fail-safe security and privacy.

About the Opportunity

As a Product Security Engineer, you will be a hands-on technical leader responsible for safeguarding the products and services that power the World project. You will be "In the Driver's Seat," proactively embedding security into every stage of the development lifecycle. This is not a role for box-tickers; you will be expected to think from first principles to solve novel security challenges at a global scale. Your work will directly protect our users and ensure the integrity of a protocol designed for the majority of humanity.

You will:

  • Lead secure architecture reviews and threat modeling sessions for new applications and services.

  • Build and operate security automation pipelines using AI agents to scale vulnerability

    detection & triage, code review, and remediation.

  • Engineer and implement automated security guardrails and reusable tools and libraries

    to make the secure path the easy path for developers.

  • Perform deep-dive, security-focused code and infrastructure reviews in languages like

    Rust, Go, and Python.

  • Own the vulnerability management process, from triaging bug bounty submissions to driving remediation efforts with engineering teams.

  • Mature and scale our Secure SDLC and bug bounty programs to keep pace with a rapidly growing engineering organization.

About You

You are a pragmatic and deeply technical security engineer who thrives on solving complex problems. You have a builder's mindset and are passionate about shipping secure products with "Extreme Urgency." You are comfortable with ambiguity and are driven by the opportunity to secure systems with world-changing potential.

  • You have 6+ years of hands-on experience in Product Security or Application Security

  • You have experience building and operating security automation pipelines using AI agents for vulnerability detection & triage, code review, and remediation.

  • You are proficient in code review and development in languages like Rust, Go, and Python.

  • You have extensive experience securing modern AWS architectures and developing secure infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform and CDK).

  • You can assess exploitability, prioritize security risks, and explain practical tradeoffs to engineering teams.

  • You have a strong background in implementing and managing security tooling (SAST, DAST, SCA) and embedding security into CI/CD pipelines.

  • You have a deep understanding of web and API security principles (OWASP Top 10) and have experience securing distributed, mobile-first systems.

Nice to have: particular interest in securing mobile applications or smart contracts.

What we offer

The reasonably estimated salary for this role at Tools for Humanity ranges from $293,000 - $325,000 plus a competitive long-term incentive package. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, Tools for Humanity offers a wide range of best-in-class, comprehensive, and inclusive employee benefits for this role, including healthcare, dental, vision, 401(k) plan and match, life insurance, flexible time off, commuter benefits, professional development stipend, and much more.

The role will lead end-to-end validation of fraud models, from conceptual soundness, data and implementation review to outcomes analysis, performance monitoring, and remediation follow-up. The portfolio may include supervised machine learning models, anomaly detection, graph and network analytics, rules-based or hybrid systems, and AI-enabled fraud applications.
 
The ideal candidate brings deep hands-on experience in fraud model validation, strong quantitative judgment, and practical experience assessing AI/ML models. This person will partner closely with Fraud, Risk, Product, Data Science, Engineering, Compliance, and Audit teams while maintaining the independence of the MRM function.

  • Practical experience with statistical and machine learning methods; proficiency in Python and SQL; working knowledge of SR 11-7 or equivalent model risk and AI governance frameworks.
  • Experience with AI/ML governance and controls, including explainability, fairness, robustness, ongoing monitoring, or generative and agentic AI applications in fraud operations.

  • Strong applied AI capability: hands-on experience evaluating or building ML/LLM-based systems in production, including prompt engineering, evaluation harnesses, fine-tuning assessment, or agentic AI workflows; able to run red-team style testing on AI applications.

Supportability sits at the vital intersection of platform safety, regulatory trust and merchant growth. Our mission is to ensure legitimate businesses can seamlessly onboard and thrive on Stripe, while proactively safeguarding the financial ecosystem from bad actors and high-risk activity.

Doing this at scale requires solving high-stakes risk challenges with precision. Deceptive merchant activity, such as transaction laundering, introduces significant threats as bad actors actively adapt to mask illicit and unsupported activities behind legitimate storefronts. Rather than relying on rigid, fragmented controls that create unnecessary friction for good users, our team builds the intelligent decision systems that systematically separate legitimate businesses from adversarial behavior, enabling Stripe to grow safely and aggressively.

What you’ll do

As a Staff Backend Engineer and Technical Lead for Supportability Decisions, you will take ownership of defining and building this new space from the ground up. You will build systems that operate at the intersection of AI/ML, distributed data processing and real-time risk decisioning. You will tackle high-ambiguity technical challenges in an adversarial threat landscape, turning broad risk policies and operational needs into resilient, high-throughput backend services and stateful decision engines. As the technical anchor in Dublin, you will set architectural patterns, mentor engineers as the team scales from its initial members to ~7 ICs, and drive technical alignment with distributed partner teams globally.

  • Lead the technical vision, system architecture and delivery of the canonical Supportability Decision Layer, establishing stateful, explainable decision APIs consumed across automated systems and human operations.

Who you are

We're looking for a technical leader who thrives in ambiguity, has deep distributed systems instincts, and is energized by building a critical platform that enables global merchant growth while safeguarding the financial ecosystem. If that sounds like you, we encourage you to apply.


Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of professional backend software engineering experience building and maintaining complex distributed systems in production.
  • Proven track record as a technical lead or staff engineer driving multi-quarter technical initiatives from ambiguous requirements to production delivery.

About the role

0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.

Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:

  • Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet

  • Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes

  • Kubernetes clusters and managed databases

  • A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps

All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs.

What you'll own

You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill.

  • Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.

  • Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.

  • Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades.

  • Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap.

  • Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps.

  • Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems.

  • Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet.

  • Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning.

  • Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform.

Our stack

Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies

Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering

Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery

Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi

CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries

Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor

Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging

Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall

AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations

Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust

Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka

Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking

Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access

Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud

Must-haves

  • We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines.

Kubernetes, in depth

  • Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions.

  • Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure.

  • Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work.

  • Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster.

  • Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables.

  • Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore.

  • Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux.

  • Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics.

CI/CD, in depth

  • Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates.

  • CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity.

  • Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing.

  • Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release.

  • Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection.

  • Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches.

  • Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets.

  • Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching.

Networking fundamentals

  • TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing.

  • DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups.

  • Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs.

  • Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs.

Also required

  • Production experience on at least two of Google Cloud, AWS and Alibaba Cloud, and willingness to learn the third quickly.

  • Terraform or Pulumi in production, plus scripting in Bash and in Python or Go.

  • A track record of cutting a cloud bill with data, through rightsizing, cleanup or commitments.

  • A security-first habit with production credentials, and clear written communication.

Nice to have

  • Running blockchain nodes in production, such as CometBFT validators and sentries, EVM archive or RPC nodes, and snapshot pipelines.

  • Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and Zero Trust at scale.

  • Alibaba Cloud on the international site, including its billing and support model.

  • Confidential computing (Intel TDX) and GPU workloads.

  • CKA or CKS certification, a FinOps certification, or experience moving a team between CI systems, such as Jenkins to GitHub Actions.

  • Go or Rust, enough to read and patch the services you operate.

What we offer

  • Purpose: The opportunity to contribute to making AI a public good

  • Growth: A self-directed environment where you can take initiative to shape your role and career

  • Compensation: Market-competitive compensation including, for most roles, exposure to pre-launch tokens

In addition, 0G Labs is committed to the health and well being of all of our team members. To that end, we provide reimbursements towards a holistic set of experiences and courses:

  • Core self: Transcendental Meditation

  • Mind: Landmark Education

  • Emotion: Art of Communication

  • Presence: Speech Coach

  • Body: Fitness, gym and exercise memberships/classes
